items.item_text: Bachelor's degree in related area and/or equivalent experience/training.
Advanced degree.
6 - 10 years of related experience.

Initiates and designs studies, summary reports and background materials including approaches, trends, sources and uses, etc., that have a significant impact on individual or multiple departments. (15% time)

Supports the design, facilitation, and continuous improvement of UCR's IT Portfolio Governance framework, providing operational leadership for intake, prioritization, scoring, and stage-gate review processes. Serves as primary support to the CIO and all governance committee chairs, ensuring structured decision-making, clear agendas, and timely follow-through on action items. Coordinates with portfolio analysts and project managers to maintain a prioritized, actionable roadmap aligned to the CIO's strategic vision. (15% time)
Handling highly complex and critical projects and leading projects of significance requiring facilitation and collaboration with representation across organizational functions. (10% time)

Acts as a senior extension of the CIO's office, supporting executive preparation for high-stakes engagements with university leadership, governance bodies, and academic units. Leads coordination and project management of cross-functional strategic IT initiatives, serving as resource integrator to advance complex programs spanning central ITS and distributed college and school IT environments. Builds and delivers strategic communications, analytical briefings, and IT perspective reports that represent the CIO's office to campus stakeholders, filling in for the CIO as appropriate. (10% time)

Directly supervises a team of project managers and portfolio analysts, providing leadership, mentorship, and performance management. Assigns and oversees work, ensures professional development, and builds team capacity to support the delivery of the ITS project portfolio. Establishes team standards for project delivery methodology, reporting, and quality, ensuring consistent practices across all managed initiatives. (10% time)

Negotiating directly to achieve solutions with high level stakeholders such as faculty, senate committee chairs, senior administrators, other UC locations, Office of the President, public agencies and the community to develop solutions to complex problems; providing briefings on key issues. (5% time)
Providing leadership in establishing a partnership with program directors within Executive's area, and with other organizational units. (5% time)
Provides a framework for policy and administrative change, developing strategies for change management to remove barriers to goal achievement. (5% time)
Participates in leadership transition planning. (5% time)

Providing strategic oversight for the development of the annual budget; determining expense priorities, recommending and implementing changes to methods, unit planning, staffing, programs and other financial activities. (5% time)
Stays well-informed and keeps abreast of higher education's current issues to provide the executive with broad perspective across the organization. (5% time)
Administers small to mid-level independent program(s); typically with broad and/or organization-wide impact. (5% time)
Performs highly complex resource research and studies for both internal department and external constituents. (5% time)

Advanced skills in short-and long-range planning, program and project management, facilitation and collaboration.
Advanced knowledge of the organization's processes, protocols and procedures.
Sound strategic thinking and consulting skills in guiding the organization toward workable strategies and solutions.
Knowledge of common organization-specific and other computer application programs.
Strong ability to focus on priorities, strategies, and vision.

Knowledge of higher education IT governance structures, UC system policies, and shared governance principles; ability to navigate complex, consensus-driven academic environments and build effective working relationships across colleges, schools, and administrative units.
Advanced ability to coach, facilitate and influence people at all levels.
Advanced ability to build and maintain relationships with a broad range of staff and members of the community.
Financial analysis and reporting techniques.

Advanced knowledge of IT portfolio and program governance frameworks, including stage-gate reviews, prioritization scoring, and investment lifecycle management in a complex higher education or enterprise environment.

Expert-level knowledge of project and program management methodologies including PMP, PfMP, Agile/Scrum, and hybrid delivery frameworks; ability to apply the right approach based on initiative complexity and organizational context.

Advanced ability to develop and deliver strategic communications, executive briefings, and analytical reports that translate complex technical concepts for non-technical audiences including senior university leadership, governance committees, and academic stakeholders.
